newsitem.title: YUGOSLAVIA: Yugo 1996 maize crop seen at 5.5 T - ministry.
newsitem.headline: Yugo 1996 maize crop seen at 5.5 T - ministry.

text.p: Yugoslavia's 1996 maize output is expected to reach 5.5 million tonnes, still less than 1995's harvest, a senior agriculture ministry official said on Thursday.
"By mid-November we had harvested five million tonnes of maize from 92 percent of the area under crop," ministry official Milan Prostran told Reuters.
"We expect to complete the harvest by the end of this week reaping a total of 5.5 million tonnes -- 200,000 tonnes below 1995's output."
Prostran said the average yield from the land already harvested was 3.7 tonnes per hectare.

But the ministry expected the yield would rise to 3.8 tonnes after bringing in the remaining 120,000-130,000 hectares in the country's bread-basket of Vojvodina -- still well below 4.15 tonnes per hectare in 1995.
Yugoslavia this year increased the area under maize to about 1.5 million hectares from 1.38 million in 1995.
According to Prostran's figures, sunflower production this year rose to about 400,000 tonnes from 204,000 hectares against 1995 output of 295,000 tonnes from 198,000 hectares.
Yugoslavia's soybean output from 72,800 hectares rose to about 150,000 tonnes from 107,000 in 1995. Last year's crop area was 52,000 hectares.
